security-events.chart_empty: No suspicious activity was recorded during the monitored period.
security-events.retention_hint: Daily automatic cleanup runs in the background. The manual cleanup on the right only deletes records older than this value - if there are none, nothing gets deleted (which is correct).

security-events.explain_login_captcha_failed_what: Someone submitted the login form without a valid CAPTCHA verification from IP address {ip} (endpoint {route}).
security-events.explain_login_captcha_failed_recommendat: If the occurrence count is rapidly increasing, this is likely an automated script trying passwords (a typical bot cannot solve the CAPTCHA). Consider temporarily blocking this IP at the firewall, hosting, or CDN level (e.g. Cloudflare).
security-events.explain_login_captcha_service_error_what: The server attempted to verify a CAPTCHA token with Cloudflare Turnstile, but the external service did not respond or returned an error.
security-events.explain_login_captcha_service_error_reco: Usually not an attack, just a temporary third-party outage. No action needed - if it persists, check Cloudflare Turnstile status.
security-events.explain_form_captcha_failed_what: Someone submitted a public web form (contact / order / job application) without a valid CAPTCHA verification from IP address {ip} (endpoint {route}). Nothing was stored.
security-events.explain_form_captcha_failed_recommendati: Single occurrences are usually ordinary visitors (expired token, blocked script). If the occurrence count is rapidly increasing, this is likely a spam bot - the form stopped it, usually no action is needed. Under a lasting flood consider blocking the IP at the firewall, hosting, or CDN level.
security-events.explain_form_captcha_service_error_what: The server attempted to verify the CAPTCHA token of a public form with Cloudflare Turnstile, but the service did not respond or returned an error. The submission was refused for safety.
security-events.explain_form_captcha_service_error_recom: Usually not an attack but a third-party outage - visitors cannot send the forms while it lasts. If it persists, check the Cloudflare Turnstile status and the TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY.
security-events.explain_form_honeypot_what: A bot submitted a public web form from IP address {ip}: it filled the hidden field a person never sees (endpoint {route}). The submission was silently dropped – nothing was stored and no e-mail was sent.
security-events.explain_form_honeypot_recommendation: No action needed, the protection worked. If the occurrence count from one IP grows rapidly, consider blocking it at the firewall, hosting, or CDN level.
security-events.explain_throttle_exceeded_what: IP address {ip} sent more requests to endpoint {route} than the configured limit allows within one minute ({occurrences}x within the monitored window).
security-events.explain_throttle_exceeded_recommendation: On public forms (inquiries, password reset) this may indicate a spam or flooding attempt. If it continues from the same IP over time, consider blocking it at the firewall/CDN level.
security-events.explain_login_failed_what: Someone attempted to log in with an incorrect password for account {email} from IP address {ip}.
security-events.explain_login_failed_recommendation: A single failed attempt is normal (a typo). Watch whether the occurrence count keeps rising - that would be a warning sign (see "Suspected brute-force attack" below).
security-events.explain_login_brute_force_suspected_what: The number of failed login attempts for account {email} from IP address {ip} has exceeded the security threshold - the system now requires CAPTCHA for this e-mail.
security-events.explain_login_brute_force_suspected_reco: We recommend checking whether the affected account has a weak/guessable password, or forcing a password change. If attempts continue even after CAPTCHA is enforced, consider blocking the IP address.
security-events.explain_login_2fa_invalid_what: User (ID {user_id}) entered an incorrect two-factor verification code after successfully logging in with a password, from IP address {ip}.
security-events.explain_login_2fa_invalid_recommendation: An isolated occurrence is usually just a typo. Multiple attempts in quick succession may mean an attacker knows the password but lacks access to the code inbox - consider contacting the user and recommending a password change.
security-events.explain_login_2fa_exhausted_what: User (ID {user_id}) repeatedly entered an incorrect verification code and exhausted the maximum allowed attempts - the login session was invalidated.
security-events.explain_login_2fa_exhausted_recommendati: We recommend confirming with the user whether they were genuinely trying to log in. If not, this is a fairly strong signal of a compromised password.
security-events.explain_login_2fa_resend_exhausted_what: The maximum number of repeated verification-code resend requests was reached within a single login session (from IP address {ip}).
security-events.explain_login_2fa_resend_exhausted_recom: Not very significant on its own. Combined with other events from the same IP or account, this may indicate an attempt to flood the user's e-mail inbox - check other records with the same IP.
security-events.explain_refresh_token_invalid_what: The application attempted to refresh a login using a token that is expired, deleted, or invalid (IP address {ip}).
security-events.explain_refresh_token_invalid_recommenda: Usually a normal session expiration (the user hasn't logged in for a while) - no action needed in that case. A high occurrence count from a single IP may indicate an attempt to guess/misuse a token - in that case, consider blocking the IP.
security-events.explain_scan_probe_what: A bot attempted to call a path that doesn't exist in this application, but is typical of known vulnerabilities in other systems (exposed .env files, old WordPress installs, an exposed .git directory, etc.) - most recently {route}, from IP address {ip}.
security-events.explain_scan_probe_recommendation: Bots do this virtually continuously across the entire internet - since such paths don't exist in this application, they are not a vulnerability on their own. If traffic from a single IP continues at high volume over time, consider a permanent block at the firewall/CDN level.
security-events.explain_csp_violation_what: A visitor's browser from IP address {ip} blocked a resource on a page that the Content-Security-Policy does not allow - {occurrences} occurrence(s). The directive, what was blocked and on which part of the site are in the detail of the record (context).
security-events.explain_refresh_token_reuse_what: A login (refresh) token of the account ID {user_id} that had already been used and replaced arrived from IP address {ip}. Two parties hold the token - one of them most likely stole it. The application therefore ended every login of this account.
security-events.explain_refresh_token_reuse_recommendati: Check with the user whether they recently signed in from another device or network. If not, have them change the password, check their devices (malware, browser extensions) and review the other security events from the same IP address.
security-events.explain_csp_violation_recommendation: A blocked inline script or an unknown foreign domain may be an attempt to inject malicious code (XSS) - the policy has just stopped it. Visitors' browser extensions often cause similar reports, which are harmless. If a domain the site itself needs (new analytics, a payment gateway) is reported repeatedly, add it to the policy in deploy/server/.htaccess.
security-events.explain_fallback_what: No detailed description is available yet for this event type.
security-events.explain_fallback_recommendation: Check the IP address, endpoint, and record context manually, or contact the developers about adding an explanation for this type.
